_comment: Which environment variables may reach each container app, where each one comes from,
and what must be true of them before scripts/cd.sh is allowed to change anything.
Rendered and enforced by scripts/deploy_env.py.
Every variable a container receives has exactly one owner:
variables    - a GitHub variable of the same name (dev environment or repository),
read from DEPLOYMENT_VARS_JSON. Visible in `gh variable list`.
derived      - computed by cd.sh (the environment name, the API's internal origin).
infra        - set by infra/bicep and carried over from the running app unchanged.
secret_refs  - bound to a Key Vault-backed secret that infra/bicep declared on the app.
secrets      - a GitHub secret (dev environment), read from DEPLOYMENT_SECRETS_JSON
and written to the named Key Vault secret, never to the container env;
the app reads it through its secret_ref.
Only names listed under variables, rename, and secrets are read from GitHub. Both
objects hold every variable and secret the run can see, most of them not app config
(AZURE_CLIENT_ID there is the deploy's sign-in app, not the API's identity), so
everything else in them is ignored, and each name is read only from its own kind.
Env is applied with --replace-env-vars, so anything on the running app that this
contract does not render is removed. cd.sh refuses that unless ALLOW_PRUNE=true.
`omitted` names Settings fields that are deliberately NOT deployable.
scripts/tests/test_env_contract.py asserts the api sections cover the Settings surface
exactly, and the web sections cover exactly the runtime env the web server reads.
Adding a setting: add the Settings field (api/app/core/config.py), give it one owner
here, and set the GitHub variable or secret. CI fails until all three agree.

derived.ENVIRONMENT: The deployment target (dev), not a per-repo choice.

infra.AZURE_CLIENT_ID: The user-assigned identity's client id, for DefaultAzureCredential (api-app.bicep).

omitted.APP_NAME: A product constant; the default is the project name.
omitted.API_V1_PREFIX: The route prefix is part of the API contract, not configuration.

rules.why: disabled is local-only; deployed, it signs every caller in as an admin.
Must point at the deployed database.

derived.BACKEND_ORIGIN: https:// + the API app's internal ingress FQDN, read from Azure.
